extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) handling after-final submissions, transitional 37 CFR 1.129(a) practice, and RCEs under 37 CFR 1.114
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural standards and eligibility rules for (a) transitional after-final submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a) and (b) Requests for Continued Examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114, including what counts as a submission, timing/fee requirements, processing, and treatment of improper/ambiguous filings. Targeted at examiners and applicants for U.S. utility/plant patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for transitional 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application is subject to the provisions of Public Law 103-465, effective June 8, 1995. Accordingly, since this application has been pending for at least two years as of June 8, 1995, taking into account any reference to an earlier filed application under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c), applicant, under 37 CFR 1.129(a), is entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits if, prior to abandonment, the submission and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) are filed prior to the filing of an appeal brief under 37 CFR 41.37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use in design or reissue applications or in reexamination proceedings. The filing date used to determine the two-year pendency counts references under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content permitted in a submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) may comprise, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement (IDS), an amendment to the written description, claims or drawings, a new substantive argument and/or new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment considered as a result of payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) may introduce new matter into the disclosure of the application (35 U.S.C. 132).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of previously-refused IDS when filing under 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any (IDS) previously refused consideration in the application because of applicant’s failure to comply with 37 CFR 1.97(c) or (d) will be treated as though it has been filed within one of the time periods set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(b) and will be considered without the petition and petition fee required in 37 CFR 1.97(d), if it complies with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS submitted under 1.129(a) on or after June 8, 2005 without a statement specified in 37 CFR 1.97(e) will be treated as though it had been filed within the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p). The examiner may introduce a new ground of rejection based on information submitted in the IDS and make the next Office action final provided no other new ground of rejection (not necessitated by an amendment) is introduced. See MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and fee requirements for 1.129(a) submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant, under 37 CFR 1.129(a), is entitled to have a submission entered and considered on the merits if the submission and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) are filed prior to abandonment and prior to the filing of an appeal brief under 37 CFR 41.37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Notice of Appeal and the appeal fee were filed prior to or with payment of the 1.17(r) fee, payment of the 1.17(r) fee will be construed as a request to dismiss the appeal and continue prosecution under 1.129(a). A conditional payment (authorization to charge deposit/credit) is treated as unconditional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting proposed amendments on 1.129(a) submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant has filed multiple proposed amendments which, when entered, would conflict with one another, specific instructions for entry or non-entry of each such amendment should be provided upon payment of any fee under 37 CFR 1.17(r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon payment of 1.17(r) fee, previously unentered submissions and newly-filed submissions will be entered in the order filed absent specific instructions. Applicants should clarify conflicting amendments when paying the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonresponsive submission after 1.129(a) filing — shortened reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner determines that the submission is not fully responsive to the previous Office action, e.g., if the submission only includes an information disclosure statement, applicant will be given a new shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS from the mailing date of this letter, whichever is longer, to submit a complete reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons why the examiner considers the submission not to be fully responsive must be set forth in the notice. This shortened period supersedes the prior Office action time period and may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If a notice of appeal and appeal fee were filed prior to or with payment of 1.17(r), payment is construed as request to dismiss appeal and continue prosecution; the appeal stands dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on number of submissions under 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant whose application is eligible for the transitional further limited examination procedure set forth in 37 CFR 1.129(a) is entitled to consideration of two after final submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one submission has been filed and the application is again under a final rejection, applicant is entitled to only one additional submission under 1.129(a). If two submissions have been filed and the application is again under final rejection, applicant is not entitled to any additional submissions under 1.129(a). Applicant may be entitled to consideration of an additional submission only if it meets conditions set forth in 37 CFR 1.116.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final action practice for submissions under 1.129(a) filed prior to June 8, 2005
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission and payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r), the next Office action on the merits may be made final only under the conditions for making a first action in a continuing application final set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.03 may be used to make the first action final following a submission under 1.129(a) filed prior to June 8, 2005. A shortened statutory period for reply to this final action is set to expire THREE MONTHS from the mailing date (with rules about filings within TWO MONTHS and max SIX MONTHS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final action practice for submissions under 1.129(a) filed on/after June 8, 2005
rubrics_metrics.description: For timely submission and payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) on or after June 8, 2005, the next Office action on the merits will be equivalent to the next Office action following a reply to a non-final Office action and, under existing second action final practice, such an Office action will be made final except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant’s amendment of the claims nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with fee 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.031 to make next Office action final when appropriate. Reminder of extension policy under 37 CFR 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE applicability (what applications qualify)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.114 apply to utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or international applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.114(e) lists exclusions: does not apply to a provisional application; an application for a utility or plant patent filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) before June 8, 1995; an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 before June 8, 1995; an application for a design patent; or a patent under reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an RCE may be filed (timing rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may obtain continued examination by filing a request for continued examination (RCE), a submission and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) prior to the earliest of: (1) payment of the issue fee unless a petition under § 1.313 is granted; (2) abandonment of the application; or (3) the filing of a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or the commencement of a civil action (unless terminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant cannot request continued examination until prosecution in the application is closed (under appeal, last OA is final, notice of allowance, or other closing action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a submission for RCE (what counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission as used in this section includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of § 1.111. A request for suspension of action, an appeal brief or a reply brief (or related papers) will not be considered a submission under this section, but a submission may incorporate by reference arguments in a previously filed appeal or reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely RCE filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant timely files a submission and fee set forth in § 1.17(e), the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action and the submission will be entered and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is filed after appeal but prior to decision, it will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner. An appeal brief or reply brief will not be considered a submission under § 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE cannot be used to 'switch inventions' (no independent and distinct claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot file an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any newly submitted claims that are directed to an invention that is independent and distinct from the invention previously claimed will be withdrawn from consideration and not entered. See 37 CFR 1.145.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing checks for RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support personnel will verify that: the RCE was filed on or after May 29, 2000; the application was filed on or after June 8, 1995; the application is a utility or plant application; the application was pending when the RCE was filed; prosecution in the application is closed; the RCE was filed before payment of the issue fee or a petition under 1.313 was granted; and the RCE was accompanied by the proper fee(s) including the RCE fee under 1.17(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more conditions are not satisfied, applicant will be notified (generally via Form PTO-2051) and an improper RCE will not toll existing time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of an improper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more conditions for filing an RCE have not been satisfied, applicant will be so notified. Generally, a 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE),' Form PTO-2051, will be mailed to applicant. An improper RCE will not operate to toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution is not closed, applicant will be notified of the improper RCE and any amendment/reply will be entered and forwarded to examiner under 1.111. If the application is under appeal and the RCE lacked fee/submission, it will be forwarded for appropriate treatment and applicant notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous transmittal papers (CPA vs RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transmittal paper is ambiguous as to whether it is a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) under 1.53(d) or an RCE under 1.114 (e.g., references to both), and the application is a plant or utility application filed on or after June 8, 1995, the Office will treat the transmittal paper as an RCE under 1.114 since CPA practice has been eliminated as to plant and utility applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is a design application, an ambiguous transmittal is treated as a CPA. Other papers filed with the transmittal (preliminary amendment, IDS) will not be taken into account in determining whether the transmittal is ambiguous. An unambiguous RCE transmittal filed in a design application will be treated as an improper RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional RCE payment treated as proper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission is accompanied by a 'conditional' RCE and payment of the RCE fee (i.e., an authorization to charge the fee to a deposit account in the event the submission would not otherwise be entered), the Office will treat the 'conditional' RCE and payment as if an RCE and payment of the fee had been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat authorization to charge deposit/credit as a valid fee payment for RCE processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and ordering of amendments with a proper RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conditions for filing an RCE have been satisfied, previously filed unentered amendments, and amendments filed with the RCE will normally be entered. Such amendments will be entered in the order in which they were filed in the absence of any specific instructions for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant filed an after-final amendment previously denied entry but later files an RCE with an amendment silent as to the prior after-final amendment, the Office will enter both amendments in order. If instructions accompany the RCE to not enter a previously-filed after-final amendment, the Office will not enter the unentered after-final amendment. Applicants are encouraged to file all amendments no later than the RCE filing to avoid disapproval of entry under 37 CFR 1.111(b). Consider filing suspension of action (37 CFR 1.103(c)) if additional time is needed for supplements (e.g., affidavits, test data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA treated as RCE and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files a request for a CPA of a utility or plant application filed on or after July 14, 2003, the Office will treat the improper CPA as an RCE of the prior application under 37 CFR 1.114. If the CPA does not satisfy requirements to be a proper RCE (e.g., lacks submission or fee), the improper CPA will be treated as an improper RCE and the time period in the last Office action will continue to run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not convert an improper CPA into an application under 1.53(b) simply because requested by applicant; conversion to 1.53(b) occurs only if applicant shows extenuating circumstances (e.g., application issued as patent and cannot be restored to pending status). Use form paragraph 7.42.15 to advise applicant a CPA is being treated as an RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment requirements when filing an RCE after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission that is an amendment must comply with the manner of making amendments as set forth in 37 CFR 1.121. The amendment must include markings showing the changes relative to the last entered amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously filed unentered after-final amendments may satisfy the submission requirement under 1.114(c), but applicants are encouraged to file an amendment at the time of filing the RCE that incorporates all desired changes and instructions regarding unentered after-final amendments. See subsection VI for treatment of not fully responsive or noncompliant amendments.
